itineraries.title: Two Plantations and a Ball Game — Durham
itineraries.theme: Morning history at the two state sites north and west of town, an afternoon of shade, then a Friday-night Bulls game
itineraries.drive_time: About 25 minutes of driving all day if you stay in Durham. Bennett Place to Stagville is the long hop — 20 minutes across the north side of town; everything after that is inside the downtown loop.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $15–$60 per person (both historic tours run $2–$4; the market is free; a Bulls ticket and dinner are the real spend)
itineraries.overview: 97°F with afternoon storms possible, so this route does its outdoor walking before noon and hides indoors from 2 to 5. Bennett Place explicitly warns that August heat shortens or cancels its later tours, which is why the 9:45 AM slot leads. The evening is a ballpark, which is the correct answer to a Durham Friday.

morning.title: Bennett Place Guided Tour
morning.location: Bennett Place State Historic Site, 4409 Bennett Memorial Rd, Durham
morning.notes: The farmhouse where Johnston surrendered to Sherman — the largest surrender of the Civil War, and a much quieter site than it deserves to be. There is an earlier 9:45 tour if you want it; the site warns that its later slots get cut in extreme heat, so earlier is safer.

afternoon.title: Historic Stagville Afternoon Guided Tour
afternoon.location: Historic Stagville State Historic Site, 5828 Old Oxford Hwy, Durham
afternoon.notes: Twenty minutes northeast. One of the largest plantations in the antebellum South, told from the perspective of the people enslaved there. The Horton Grove quarters they built are still standing. Mostly outdoors — bring water and a hat.

afternoon.title: North Durham Friday Evening Farmers' Market
afternoon.notes: The Friday-evening edition. Exact hours aren't published on the listing, so treat 4 PM as approximate and check before you drive over.

evening.title: Live Music with Tom Neuhauser
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham
evening.notes: Skip this one if you're going to the ballgame — it's 15 minutes the wrong way. Included as the alternative evening if baseball isn't your thing: solo set in the beer garden, no cover mentioned.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Memphis Redbirds
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: Friday home game against Memphis. Gates typically open an hour early; the third-base side gets shade first on a hot night.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan doughnuts are made daily and the bagel sandwiches can be built without egg or cheese — ask which doughnut flavors are vegan that morning, it rotates
food.notes: 1002 9th St. Open early, which matters when you're aiming for a 9:45 tour on the other side of town. Order ahead on a Friday.

food.vegan_dish: Arepa or bowl with black beans, plantains, avocado and the guasacaca sauce — build it without cheese or crema
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese arepa with plantains and the full sauce bar
food.notes: Fast, cheap, air-conditioned, and everything is built to order at the counter, so dietary swaps are easy. A good reset after two hours in the sun at Stagville.

food.vegan_dish: Work the stalls — at least one counter usually plates a fully vegan bowl or sandwich; ask each vendor directly since the lineup rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza or a vegetable-forward plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 530 Foster St, a seven-minute walk from the DBAP. Multiple kitchens under one roof solves the group-can't-agree problem, and you can eat before first pitch without a reservation.

alternatives.good_weather: Do the full walk to Horton Grove and the great barn.
alternatives.rain: The tour runs in light rain but the site is exposed. If storms build, swap to the Nasher Museum of Art on Duke's campus — indoors, air-conditioned, 20 minutes south.

alternatives.good_weather: Sit in the outfield grass berm if it's available; it's the cheapest seat and catches the evening breeze.
alternatives.rain: Storms are only a slight chance Friday, but rain delays happen. The Carolina Theatre is eight minutes away and running the OUTSOUTH Queer Film Festival through Sunday — a real indoor backup, $15 a film.

practical_notes: Both state historic sites are free to enter; you only pay for the guided tour, and both take cash or card at the desk.
Bennett Place and Stagville are closed Sunday and Monday — this itinerary only works Tuesday through Saturday.
97°F. The Stagville tour is 90 minutes largely in the open; carry more water than you think you need.
DBAP parking decks fill by 6:15 on a Friday. The Church Street deck is a five-minute walk and usually has room.
Tickets for the Bulls are worth buying ahead on a weekend homestand, even though walk-up is usually possible.

itineraries.title: Market, Violin, Giant Puppets — Carrboro & Chapel Hill
itineraries.theme: A Saturday that starts at 7 AM in a farmers market and ends under stilt-walkers in an outdoor amphitheater
itineraries.drive_time: Park in Carrboro and barely move. The Town Commons, The ArtsCenter and Weaver Street are within four blocks; Forest Theatre is a 10-minute drive or a 25-minute walk east through campus.

weather.summary: Partly Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $40–$90 per person (market and morning are free; the $30 ArtsCenter concert and Paperhand tickets are the spend)
itineraries.overview: Saturday is the coolest day of the week at 93°F, with a real chance of afternoon thunderstorms. This route uses that shape: outdoors early, an air-conditioned concert in the hot part of the day, then back outdoors at 7 for Paperhand's 26th summer show at the Forest Theatre.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers Market
morning.location: Carrboro Town Commons, 301 W Main St, Carrboro
morning.notes: Opens at 7, which is early for a reason in August — the good tomatoes and the shade are both gone by 10. One of the oldest producer-only markets in the state.

morning.title: Magic Tree House Space Mission
morning.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
morning.notes: Ten minutes east. The kid-scale dome show — 45 minutes, fully air-conditioned. Skip if you're not travelling with children and go straight to lunch.

afternoon.title: Messengers of Time & Space
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: The grown-up companion show if you're staying at the planetarium. Otherwise this is your lunch window.

afternoon.title: Jennifer Curtis with Gabriel Pelli
afternoon.notes: Back in Carrboro. Violinist Jennifer Curtis in the black-box theater — 90-ish minutes, indoors, and timed exactly for when the storms are most likely.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Project: The Wild Wisdom of the World
evening.location: Forest Theatre, 123 South Boundary St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Paperhand's 26th annual summer show, in a stone amphitheater built in 1940. Openers at 6:20, Paperhand at 7. ASL interpretation is provided tonight. Lawn chairs are not allowed — bring a blanket or a cushion.

food.vegan_dish: The hot bar and salad bar both label vegan items, and the bakery keeps vegan pastries — assemble a plate and eat it on the lawn
food.vegetarian_dish: Breakfast burrito or a pastry and coffee from the bakery counter
food.notes: 101 E Weaver St, right beside the market. Buy at the counter, eat outside on the lawn. This is what Carrboro does on a Saturday morning.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala or the vegetable curry of the day — the kitchen cooks a large share of the menu vegan and marks it clearly
food.vegetarian_dish: Palak paneer with rice and naan
food.notes: 431 W Franklin St, in Courtyard. Long-running, generous with dietary questions, and cool inside — a good landing spot between the planetarium and the concert.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for the veggie patty built without cheese or mayo — confirm the bun at the counter
food.notes: 516 W Franklin St. Fast and close to Forest Theatre, which matters when the show starts at 7 and parking near the amphitheater is thin. Eat by 6.

alternatives.leg: Carrboro Farmers Market (7 AM, open air)
alternatives.good_weather: Go at 7, walk the full row twice, then take coffee to the Weaver Street lawn.
alternatives.rain: The market runs rain or shine under vendor tents. If it's heavy, Weaver Street Market itself is 100 feet away and indoors.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand at Forest Theatre (7 PM, fully outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Arrive by 6:20 for the opening act and to get a seat on the stone terraces.
alternatives.rain: Forest Theatre has no cover. If it storms, Film Night at The ArtsCenter runs Sunday at 7 PM for $10, and the ComedyWorx Varsity show in Raleigh starts at 7 tonight — check Paperhand's channels before you drive, as they call weather late.

practical_notes: Paperhand tickets sell through Ticket Tailor and are non-refundable — buy ahead, and read their FAQ about seating before you do.
Forest Theatre parking is street-only along Country Club Road and fills 45 minutes before curtain. Budget the walk.
The ArtsCenter concert is $30 plus fees and seats are limited in the black box; don't plan on walking up.
93°F with storms possible from mid-afternoon — the two indoor legs at noon and 3 PM are deliberate.
Carrboro parking is free on Saturdays in the town lots off Main Street.

itineraries.title: Mud, Mas and an Amphitheater — Raleigh Saturday
itineraries.theme: A free morning in a wetland mud pit, a Caribbean carnival downtown, and a stadium show to close it out
itineraries.drive_time: Roughly 30 minutes of driving total. Walnut Creek to downtown is 10 minutes; park downtown once after that and walk the rest.

weather.summary: Partly Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$120 per person (Mud Day, the market and SCRUMFEST are free; only the Red Hat show and food cost anything)
itineraries.overview: Two of the best free events of the week land on the same Saturday in Raleigh, and they're ten minutes apart. Mud Day is genuinely a giant mud slide for kids at a wetland park; CaribMask is the city's Afro-Caribbean carnival with a parade on a new route. Both are outdoors on a 93°F day with storms possible late, so eat and rest indoors between them.

morning.title: Midtown Farmers' Market
morning.location: The Commons at North Hills, 4150 Main at North Hills St, Raleigh
morning.notes: Optional opener if you're up early. Ends at noon, and it's the opposite direction from Mud Day — only worth it if you're already north.

morning.title: Mud Day
morning.location: Walnut Creek Wetland Park, 950 Peterson St, Raleigh
morning.notes: The 8th annual wetlands festival. There is an actual giant mud pit and children slide into it. Bring a full change of clothes, a towel, and a trash bag for the car seat. Runs to 1 PM.

afternoon.title: SCRUMFEST
afternoon.location: Compass Rose Brewery, 3201 Northside Dr, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Nine bands, free entry, noon to 9 PM. This is the low-key alternative to the carnival if you'd rather sit in one place all afternoon with a beer.

afternoon.title: CaribMask Caribbean Carnival
afternoon.notes: Runs 11 AM to 8 PM with mas bands and a costumed parade on a new route this year. Arrive mid-afternoon for the parade and the food vendors; the music runs late.

evening.title: Simple Plan: Bigger Than You Think! Tour - The Sequel
evening.location: Red Hat Amphitheater, 500 S McDowell St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Six blocks from the carnival footprint, so you can walk straight over. Outdoor amphitheater — no re-entry once you're in.

evening.title: TK Productions Presents: MavicMachine
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, 224 S Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The late option if the amphitheater isn't your bill. Doors at 8, four blocks north of Red Hat.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk drinks and the avocado toast built without egg — ask about the bread, which changes
food.vegetarian_dish: Biscuit with egg and cheese, or the granola bowl
food.notes: 8450 Honeycutt Rd or the Hillsborough Street shop. Get it to go; you want to be at Walnut Creek by 10 before the mud pit line builds.

food.vegan_dish: The falafel and hummus counters plate vegan without substitutions — confirm with the individual stall, as the vendor lineup rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Wood-fired margherita pizza or a cheese-and-vegetable sandwich from the deli
food.notes: 500 E Davie St, air-conditioned, and the natural place to clean up and cool off between Mud Day and the carnival. Bathrooms are decent, which matters after a mud pit.

food.vegan_dish: Look for a doubles or channa stand — Trinidadian doubles are vegan by default; ask about the chutneys
food.vegetarian_dish: Roti with pumpkin and channa, or fried plantain
food.notes: Eating the carnival's own food is the point. If the vendor lines are impossible, Garland at 14 W Martin St does excellent vegetarian Indian-Southern plates five minutes away.

alternatives.good_weather: Go at 10 sharp. Free, no ticket, and the mud is best before the crowd doubles at 11.
alternatives.rain: Mud Day and rain are not enemies, but lightning closes it. Indoor swap: NCMA Games Together runs 10 AM to 10 PM the same day, free to enter, with a D&D intro at noon.

alternatives.leg: Simple Plan at Red Hat (7 PM, open-air amphitheater)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk over from downtown; the McDowell Street gate is quickest from the carnival.
alternatives.rain: Red Hat shows continue through light rain and only stop for lightning. The indoor backup four blocks away is MavicMachine at the Pour House at 9 PM for $17.88.

practical_notes: Mud Day is free with no registration. Change of clothes, towel, sunscreen, water. The parking lot at Walnut Creek is small — arrive early or park on Peterson Street.
CaribMask's parade route changed this year and the website doesn't post a start time; check their channels the morning of.
Red Hat Amphitheater is clear-bag only and has no re-entry.
Downtown decks are free on Saturdays; the Moore Square deck sits between the carnival and both music venues.
93°F with thunderstorms possible from mid-afternoon. Every leg here has an indoor twin within ten minutes.

itineraries.title: Second Friday, Slowly — Chapel Hill
itineraries.theme: A museum tour, a library movie, extended gallery hours and three hours of free porch music
itineraries.drive_time: Park once on Franklin Street and walk. The Ackland, the Carolina Inn and Franklin Street are within six blocks; the library is a five-minute drive north.

weather.summary: Mostly Sunny then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 per person (the Ackland, the library and the porch music are all free; you pay for food and, if you add it, Paperhand)
itineraries.overview: 97°F, the hottest Friday of the week, so this is the itinerary built almost entirely out of free, air-conditioned, indoor things — with one shaded outdoor finish. Second Friday ArtWalk keeps the Ackland open until 9 PM, and the Carolina Inn's front porch series runs 5 to 8 with the Adam Lee Decker Band.

afternoon.title: Tour: A Closer Look at Continental Shift
afternoon.location: Ackland Art Museum, 101 S Columbia St, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Thirty minutes, free, focused on a handful of works rather than the whole museum. A good way into the Continental Shift show without committing an afternoon.

afternoon.title: Family Movie at Chapel Hill Public Library
afternoon.location: Chapel Hill Public Library, 100 Library Dr, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Free, indoors, and 105 minutes of air conditioning in the worst heat of the day. Skip if you're not travelling with kids and stay at the Ackland instead.

evening.title: Fridays on the Front Porch: Adam Lee Decker Band
evening.location: The Carolina Inn, 211 Pittsboro St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Five to eight on the Inn's covered porch and lawn, with food and drink service. Covered is the operative word on a day with a chance of storms.

evening.title: 2nd Friday ArtWalk: Extended Museum Hours
evening.location: Ackland Art Museum, 101 S Columbia St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: The Ackland stays open to 9 PM, free. Two blocks from the Carolina Inn — you can do both, drifting between them.

evening.title: Family Fun Friday at Chapel Hill Public Library
evening.location: Chapel Hill Public Library, 100 Library Dr, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: The kid alternative to the porch, 6 to 8 PM and free.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Project: The Wild Wisdom of the World
evening.location: Forest Theatre, 123 South Boundary St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Optional big finish, ten minutes east. ASL interpretation tonight. If you add this, leave the porch by 6:15 to park.

food.vegan_dish: Build a plate from the mezze case — falafel, hummus, baba ghanoush, tabbouleh and stuffed grape leaves are all vegan; the staff will tell you which of the day's specials aren't
food.notes: 410 W Franklin St. Enormous vegetarian and vegan range, counter service, and cold inside. Probably the single easiest plant-based lunch on this list.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the kitchen for the vegetable plate built without butter — they do it, but you have to ask
food.vegetarian_dish: The seasonal vegetable and grain plate, or a cheese board on the porch
food.notes: Eating where you're already sitting is the whole appeal of the porch series. Cheaper alternative: Sup Dogs or Al's Burger Shack on Franklin, both five minutes' walk.

alternatives.leg: Fridays on the Front Porch (5 PM, outdoors but covered)
alternatives.good_weather: Take the lawn; the porch fills first and the lawn catches whatever breeze there is.
alternatives.rain: The porch itself is roofed, so light rain is fine. In a real storm the Ackland is two blocks away and open free until 9.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand at Forest Theatre (7 PM, no cover)
alternatives.good_weather: Add it — it's the best outdoor show in the county this month.
alternatives.rain: No shelter at Forest Theatre. Drop it and stay at the Ackland, or drive 15 minutes to Local 506 for the tenderqueer single release party at 8 PM.

practical_notes: The Ackland is free always, and free parking is available in the Wilson Street lot after 5 PM on Fridays.
Fridays on the Front Porch has no ticket and no cover; you pay only for food and drink.
97°F. The 1 PM to 5 PM block here is deliberately all indoors.
Chapel Hill Public Library programs are free and don't require registration, but rooms have capacity limits — arrive a few minutes early.
If you add Paperhand, buy tickets in advance through Ticket Tailor; they're non-refundable and shows do sell out.

itineraries.title: Hippie Fest to Kickoff — A Raleigh & Cary Sunday
itineraries.theme: A free retro festival in Moore Square, a museum afternoon, then a choice between a park concert and an NWSL match
itineraries.drive_time: About 40 minutes of driving across the day. Downtown Raleigh to the NCMA is 15 minutes; NCMA to WakeMed Soccer Park in Cary is 20.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$60 per person (Hippie Fest, the NCMA tour and the Pullen Park concert are free; a Courage ticket starts at $27)
itineraries.overview: 95°F and no rain in the forecast — the one fully dry day this week, which makes the evening outdoor options safe to plan around. The day splits cleanly: free festival in the morning, museum in the heat, and then either a free park concert or NWSL soccer at 7.

morning.title: All Things Groovy Hippie Fest
morning.location: Moore Square, 200 S Blount St, Raleigh
morning.notes: Free, 11 to 4, in Moore Square — tie-dye, vintage vendors and live music. Moore Square has real tree cover, which is the difference between pleasant and unbearable at 95°F.

morning.title: Sunday Brunch Music on the Lawn
morning.location: Weaver Street Market, 101 E Weaver St, Carrboro
morning.notes: The Carrboro alternative if you'd rather start west. Free music on the lawn, 11 to 1, with brunch from the market counter.

afternoon.title: Pop-Up Art: Botanical Collage
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Drop-in art-making, noon to 3, all ages. Fifteen minutes west of Moore Square and fully air-conditioned.

afternoon.title: Public Tour
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Free hour-long docent tour of collection highlights. Pairs neatly with the collage session — do one, then the other.

afternoon.title: Black Farmers Market Durham
afternoon.location: Durham Technical Community College, 1637 E Lawson St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Third-Sunday market, 1 to 4. A worthwhile detour if you're anchoring in Durham instead — 25 minutes from downtown Raleigh.

evening.title: Summer Concert Series: Bull City Trio
evening.notes: Free on the Pullen Park event lawn, 6 to 8. Bring a blanket or a chair; the cafe sells food. The relaxed close to the day.

evening.title: North Carolina Courage vs. Houston Dash
evening.location: WakeMed Soccer Park, 201 Soccer Park Dr, Cary
evening.notes: The bigger-ticket alternative. NWSL soccer in Cary, 20 minutes from the NCMA. Pick this or Pullen Park, not both.

evening.title: Art of Cool Presents The Frequency Series featuring Jonathan Butler & Najee
evening.location: Koka Booth Amphitheatre, 8003 Regency Pkwy, Cary
evening.notes: Third option, also in Cary: smooth jazz on the Koka Booth lawn by the lake. The venue page doesn't publish a start time, so confirm before you drive.

food.vegan_dish: Limited — the vegetable sides can work but most are cooked with pork; ask, and be ready to go elsewhere
food.vegetarian_dish: A plate of the vegetable sides: stewed tomatoes, mac and cheese, biscuits
food.notes: 220 Wolfe St, a two-minute walk from Moore Square. Cash-friendly Southern breakfast. If the group needs solid vegan options, walk instead to Fount Coffee or Transfer Co.

food.vegan_dish: The kitchen keeps at least one vegan plate and will adapt the vegetable dishes — ask the server, they're used to it
food.vegetarian_dish: Seasonal vegetable plate or the grain bowl
food.notes: Inside the museum, so you don't lose the air conditioning. Cheaper: the Museum Park cafe, or drive five minutes to Village District.

food.place: Pullen Park cafe or Cary's Fenton district
food.vegan_dish: At Fenton, Colletta and the food hall counters both do vegan pasta or bowls on request; at Pullen the cafe is snack-level only
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese pizza or a vegetable pasta at Fenton; ice cream and a pretzel at Pullen
food.notes: Which one depends on your evening pick. Pullen Park concert: eat light at the cafe. Courage match or Koka Booth: Fenton is ten minutes from both.

alternatives.leg: Hippie Fest at Moore Square (11 AM, outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Mostly sunny and no rain forecast — this is the safest outdoor bet of the week. Use the tree line on the north side.
alternatives.rain: Not expected Sunday. If it turns, the NCMA opens the same day and the Pour House runs a free Weezer listening party at 3 PM.

alternatives.leg: Evening: Pullen Park vs WakeMed Soccer Park (6-7 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Either works. Pullen is free and shaded; the Courage match is the bigger event.
alternatives.rain: Both are open-air. The indoor fallback is Film Night at The ArtsCenter in Carrboro at 7 PM, $10, or Owen & The Smokes at Local 506 at 8.

practical_notes: Sunday is the only fully dry day in the window — put your must-do outdoor plans here.
The NCMA is free to enter; only special exhibitions charge. Parking is free.
Moore Square parking decks are free on Sundays.
Courage tickets start around $27 and are cheaper in advance than at the gate.
95°F. Even on a dry day, the 12-4 block belongs indoors.

itineraries.title: Cheap Beer to a Murder Mystery Museum — Durham Thursday
itineraries.theme: A $5 mystery pour at lunch, a plantation tour, an art-history talk and a museum that stays open past dark
itineraries.drive_time: About 35 minutes of driving across the day, all inside Durham County. RTP to Bennett Place is the longest single hop at 20 minutes.

weather.summary: Forecast beyond the 7-day National Weather Service horizon at generation time

itineraries.cost_range: $10–$50 per person (the beer is $5, the tour is $4, the Nasher talk is free with admission; AfterHours is the one real ticket)
itineraries.overview: The last day in the window, and the one with the strongest evening. Three things converge after 6 PM in Durham: a Nasher gallery talk connecting a sculpted head in their collection to Notre-Dame, the Museum of Life and Science's prom-themed AfterHours, and the weekly Pony Run. Note that this date sits past the NWS forecast horizon, so no weather is attached to the outdoor legs — check before you commit to the run.

morning.title: Mystery Beer Thursdays
morning.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham
morning.notes: Bartender's choice for $5, all day. A cheap, low-commitment start — and the RTP taproom is quiet on a weekday morning.

morning.title: Historic Stagville Guided Tour
morning.location: Historic Stagville State Historic Site, 5828 Old Oxford Hwy, Durham
morning.notes: The serious morning alternative. Ninety minutes, mostly outdoors, $2. Second tour at 1 PM if you'd rather sleep in.

afternoon.title: Bennett Place Afternoon Guided Tour
afternoon.location: Bennett Place State Historic Site, 4409 Bennett Memorial Rd, Durham
afternoon.notes: Last tour of the day. In August the site sometimes shortens or cancels this slot for heat — call 919-383-4345 before you drive out.

evening.title: Gallery Talk: A Lost Sculpture from Notre-Dame Cathedral at the Nasher
evening.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
evening.notes: Professor Jennifer Feltman on the research linking a mysterious sculpted head in the Nasher's collection to Notre-Dame. One hour, and the kind of talk that justifies the whole evening.

evening.title: Pony Run Thursdays with Fleet Feet
evening.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co., 219 Hood St, Durham
evening.notes: Free 3-mile or 5-mile group run that ends back at the brewery. Pick this or the Nasher talk — they overlap.

evening.title: AfterHours: Mystery at the Museum
evening.location: Museum of Life and Science, 433 W Murray Ave, Durham
evening.notes: Prom-themed adult evening with the exhibits open until 10. Ten minutes north of the Nasher, so the 6 PM talk and this can just about stack if you leave promptly at 7.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan bibimbap or the tofu-based Korean plates — the kitchen marks vegan items and is careful about fish sauce
food.notes: 2812 Erwin Rd. Between RTP and the historic sites, and close to Duke. Fast enough for a midday stop.

food.vegan_dish: Depends entirely on the food truck parked outside — Ponysaurus doesn't have a kitchen; check their calendar for the night's truck
food.vegetarian_dish: Same caveat; the trucks that rotate through usually have at least one vegetarian option
food.notes: 219 Hood St. Excellent patio, no kitchen. If you need a certainty, Guglhupf on Hillsborough Road does a reliable vegetarian dinner ten minutes away.

alternatives.leg: Bennett Place afternoon tour (1 PM, largely outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Take it. The 1 PM is the least crowded slot of the day.
alternatives.rain: Call first — this slot is the one they cut for weather. The indoor swap is the Nasher, which is open Thursday and free to Duke visitors on select days.

alternatives.good_weather: Run the 5-mile route; the group splits by pace at the start.
alternatives.rain: The run is cancelled in storms but the brewery stays open. AfterHours at the Museum of Life and Science is largely indoors and runs to 10.

practical_notes: No forecast is attached to this day: August 20 falls past the National Weather Service's 7-day horizon at the time this was generated. Check the forecast yourself before the outdoor legs.
Bennett Place and Stagville both close at 5 PM and are shut Sunday and Monday.
AfterHours at the Museum of Life and Science is an adult evening event — check the age policy and whether it needs advance tickets.
The Nasher talk is listed without a price; the museum's general admission policy applies.
Ponysaurus has no kitchen. Plan food around the truck, or eat before you come.

itineraries.title: Midweek, Free and Mostly Outdoors — Durham & Carrboro
itineraries.theme: A Wednesday built entirely from free things: a garden walk, two afternoon markets, a samba drum rehearsal and a chess club
itineraries.drive_time: Duke Gardens to Carrboro is 25 minutes; if you stay in Durham it's under 10 minutes of driving all day.

weather.summary: Slight Chance Rain Showers then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$35 per person (everything on the schedule is free or free to enter; the only spend is food, drinks and whatever the market tempts you into)
itineraries.overview: The coolest day of the window at 92°F, with only a slight chance of showers. Almost nothing on this route costs money: a free lunchtime garden stroll, the two Wednesday farmers markets, Batala's open-air drum rehearsal and a drop-in chess club. It's the itinerary for a week where everything else costs $30 a ticket.

morning.title: Meditation at Dix Park
morning.location: The Chapel at Dix Park, 2105 Umstead Dr, Raleigh
morning.notes: Raleigh-side opener if you're starting from the east — an hour of guided meditation in the park's chapel. Skip if you're anchoring in Durham.

morning.title: Historic Stagville Guided Tour
morning.location: Historic Stagville State Historic Site, 5828 Old Oxford Hwy, Durham
morning.notes: The one paid thing here, and it's $2. Ninety minutes north of downtown Durham.

afternoon.title: Midday Meander
afternoon.location: Sarah P. Duke Gardens, 420 Anderson St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Forty-five free minutes walking the gardens with Kavanah Anderson. Meets at the gardens; the shaded paths make this bearable even at midday.

afternoon.title: Durham Farmers' Market Wednesday Market
afternoon.location: Durham Farmers' Market at Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
afternoon.notes: The smaller midweek market under the pavilion, 3 to 6. Less crowded than Saturday and the produce is the same.

afternoon.title: Carrboro Farmers Market Wednesday Market
afternoon.location: Carrboro Town Commons, 301 W Main St, Carrboro
afternoon.notes: The Orange County alternative, same hours. Pick one — they're 25 minutes apart and both close at 6.

evening.title: Durham Chess Club
evening.location: Durham Food Hall, 530 Foster St, Durham
evening.notes: Drop-in, all levels, indoors and air-conditioned. Fifty steps from the farmers market pavilion, so this follows the market without moving the car.

evening.title: Batala Drumming Practice
evening.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
evening.notes: Batala Durham's Afro-Brazilian samba-reggae corps rehearses in the open at the park. You can hear it from three blocks away and it's free to stand and watch.

evening.title: Camacho with Late Night Lowlights and Boost
evening.location: Local 506, 506 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: If you took the Carrboro fork in the afternoon, this is the natural close — five minutes from the Town Commons. Doors at 7.

food.vegan_dish: At Parizäde the mezze plate works vegan — hummus, baba ghanoush, dolma; confirm no yogurt in the day's dips
food.vegetarian_dish: The gardens cafe keeps simple vegetarian sandwiches and salads; Parizäde does an excellent vegetarian pasta
food.notes: The cafe is inside the gardens and saves you a drive before the 12:15 walk. Parizäde is five minutes away in Erwin Square if you want a real sit-down.

food.vegan_dish: Ask each counter — the lineup rotates but there is usually at least one fully vegan bowl or sandwich available
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, or a vegetable plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 530 Foster St, the same building as the chess club and 100 feet from the drumming. Eat, play, then walk out to the noise.

alternatives.leg: Midday Meander at Duke Gardens (12:15 PM, outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Take the full walk; the shaded lower paths near the pond are the coolest part of the gardens.
alternatives.rain: Only a slight chance Wednesday. If it lands, the Nasher Museum is six minutes away and the Duke Chapel is free to enter.

alternatives.leg: Batala drumming in Durham Central Park (7 PM, open air)
alternatives.good_weather: Stand near the pavilion end; the sound carries best there.
alternatives.rain: Rehearsal moves or cancels in weather. Indoor swap within a block: the chess club runs to 8:30 in the Food Hall, or drive 25 minutes to Local 506 for Camacho at 8.

practical_notes: Every scheduled item except the Stagville tour is free or free to enter.
Sarah P. Duke Gardens is free; parking in the gardens lot is paid and fills at lunchtime. Street parking on Anderson is the workaround.
The Durham and Carrboro Wednesday markets both run 3 to 6 and are 25 minutes apart — this route asks you to pick one.
92°F, the mildest day of the window, with only a slight chance of showers.
Durham Central Park parking is free on the Foster Street side after 5 PM.
